items.text: REFERRED TO COMMERCE, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND SMALL BUSINESS

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4437

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the economic development law, in relation to the
preparation of performance plans and the establishment of a private
industry review council; and providing for the repeal of article 7-A
of such law relating to the establishment of the New York state
private industry review council upon expiration thereof

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :
Requires economic development performance plans and evaluations and
establishes the New York State Private Industry Review Council.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

§ 1- Amends subdivision 19 of § 100 of the Economic Development Law.

§ 2- Amends the Economic Development Law by adding a new Article 7-A.

§ 3- Amends subdivision 1 of § 196 of the Economic Development Law.

§ 4- Amends paragraph (b) of subdivision 7 of § 202 of the Economic
Development Law.

§ 5- Amends the opening paragraph of subdivision 2 and paragraph (a) 3
of § 213 of the Economic Development Law.

§ 6- Amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 3 of § 223 of the Economic
Development Law.

§ 7- Amends subdivisions 9 and 10 of § 224 of the Economic Development
Law.

§ 8- Amends subdivisions 4 and 5 of § 225 of the Economic Development
Law.

§ 9- Amends paragraph (a) of subdivision 9 of § 250 of the Economic
Development Law.

§ 10- Effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :
This legislation seeks to accomplish two related goals.  First, it
establishes a Private Industry Review Council charged with the duty of
conducting a complete and thorough review of current state economic
development financial and business assistance programs and submitting
a report to the Governor and the Legislature recommending changes
necessary to eliminate duplication and streamline/reorganize economic
development programs and services.  Second, this legislation requires
that the state's major economic development agencies develop and
implement performance planning techniques which will be used to judge
the utility and effectiveness of economic development programs.
Essentially, performance planning requires that goals be set to
establish the level of performance or results to be achieved by a
particular program and that the goals established be defined in
measurable, quantifiable terms. Performance indicators are then
designed and used to assess the extent to which actual program results
meet the established program goals.

The State of New York expends millions of dollars each year on
economic development programs designed to enhance the economic well
being of the state. Unfortunately, the present economic development
system is a confusing patchwork of programs which lack coherence and
create impediments to full program utilization by the business
community.  This legislation will, through the establishment of a
Private Industry Review Council, provide the private sector a crucial
role in "reinventing" economic development programs and services.
Nowhere in state government is meaningful private sector involvement
more important or appropriate than in the delivery of programs and
services intended to enhance and promote economic development. This
legislation creates a forum for a detailed and specific private sector
review of existing economic development programs and services and
directs that recommendations be made regarding the retention,
modifications, consolidation or elimination of each such program or
service. The Council's recommendations are intended to provide private
sector input on ways to promote economy, efficiency and improved
delivery of economic development programs:  Performance planning as
required by this bill seeks to bring private sector concepts to bear
on the actual delivery of economic development programs and services
by requiring that performance plans be prepared for each financial and
business assistance program administered by the Department of Economic
Development, Urban Development Corporation, Job Development Authority
and Science and Technology Foundation. Given the importance of
economic development efforts and the large sums of state funds
involved, performance planning is critical to assuring that economic
development programs are performing as intended and achieving the
results envisioned.  This legislation will strengthen and improve
program and service delivery by bringing the private sector, and
private sector principles and techniques, into the economic
development system.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007-2008: A.3135-A; 2005-2006: A.3188; 2003-2004:  A.3470; 2001-2002:
A.1004-B; 1999-2000: A.1925-A; 1997-1998: A.5416-A; 1995-1996:
A.3728-A; 1993-1994: A.8197-A/S.616-B.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately; provided that the provisions
of Article 7-A of the Economic Development Law, added by section two
of this act, shall take effect on the first of September next
succeeding the date on which it shall have become a law and shall
expire and be deemed repealed 2 years after such effective date; and
provided further that, insofar as the amendment of sections 223, 224,
and 225 of the Economic Development Law made by sections six, seven
and eight, respectively, of this act pertain to the Port Authority of
New York and New Jersey, each shall respectively apply to such Port
Authority only upon the enactment into law by the state of New Jersey
of legislation having an identical effect with sections six, seven and
eight of this act, respectively, but if the state of New Jersey shall
have already enacted such legislation, the corresponding section of
this act shall apply to such Port Authority immediately provided that
the Commissioner of Economic Development shall notify the Legislative
Bill Drafting Commission upon the occurrence of the enactment of the
legislation provided for in sections six, seven and eight of this act
in order that the commission may maintain an accurate and timely
effective data base of the official text of the laws of the stat of
New York in furtherance of effectuating the provisions of section 44
of the Legislative Law and section 70-b of the Public Officers Law.

items.name: Commerce, Economic Development And Small Business

summary: Directs the commissioner of economic development to prepare performance plans covering financial and business assistance programs and reports thereon; establishes a private industry review council to review existing economic development programs and report as to the delivery of services thereunder.
title: Requires economic development program performance plans and evaluations; establishes private industry review council
